headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and overlapping write privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A uses MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent B exposes files, MCP, and stdin/stdout plus a self-isolation note that still leaves shared-machine surfaces. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path if B ingests A’s outputs or shared files. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF agent_b reads content produced by agent_a from shared files or MCP messages
IF either agent treats the other agent's output as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate working directories and MCP endpoints
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add provenance tags to inter-agent messages
Review any shared hooks or commands before enabling
requires-engineering: enforce message authentication between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches task prompts, repository metadata, and code; agent B touches session summaries, hooks, agent definitions, security findings, and files under ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc. Because B can read and write filesystem state and both use MCP/stdio, sensitive context can flow across a shared workspace. This is a default-path concern, not a provable exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same home directory or workspace
IF agent_b uploads or syncs files it reads from shared paths
mitigations: Use separate OS users or home directories
Move secrets out of shared paths
Restrict B's file access to a dedicated workspace
Audit MCP configs for secret-bearing mounts
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP; B also writes the filesystem. On a shared repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other, and B’s explicit shared-state warning confirms the collision risk. This is a default-dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible repo corruption.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout or filesystem root
IF either agent runs package installs or git operations without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or worktrees
Serialize git and package operations with a lock
Disable one agent's write path in shared sessions
Use per-agent scratch directories
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate analysis, route/explain/build-agents outputs, and B has skills, hooks, and security-findings surfaces that may consume upstream outputs. That makes an unverified handoff plausible, but the profiles do not prove B blindly executes A. I rate medium because the pathway exists in default workflows yet a verification step could interrupt it.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input without a verification step
IF A-produced findings are forwarded into B's hooks or skills workflow
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require citations before B acts on A's output
Limit B to read-only summarization of A outputs
Flag low-confidence A outputs automatically
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles Ed25519 signatures and repository metadata; agent B handles GitHub App Install, GitHub App OAuth, and retention-related secrets. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or regulated-data mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documented policy gaps rather than a clear breach. I do not cite both agents because this is a policy-mismatch assessment, not a direct interaction pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B's GitHub App or retention settings
IF A's signature material is stored in B-managed files or logs
mitigations: Review retention settings before enabling shared workflows
Keep signature material out of B-managed directories
Confirm GitHub App scopes are minimal
Document data-class handling for both agents
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls end-to-end
